structure.title: An education meets events
structure.text: Candide leaves his sheltered setting and carries its explanations into encounters they are poorly equipped to handle.

structure.title: Repeated trials of explanation
structure.text: Rapid journeys, reversals, and different companions test ways of explaining suffering and deciding how to live.

people.name: Candide
people.text: A naive young man raised in a German baron's castle, thrown out for kissing the baron's daughter, and sent into a world of war, earthquakes and swindlers.

people.name: Pangloss
people.text: Candide's tutor, who teaches that this is the best of all possible worlds and goes on teaching it, whatever disaster befalls them.

people.name: Cunégonde
people.text: The baron's daughter, whom Candide loves and keeps losing and finding again across continents, each time in worse circumstances.

context.title: Philosophical optimism
context.text: The target is an explanation claiming that the world's arrangement is ultimately best, not simply a cheerful mood or hope for improvement.
context.takeaway: Distinguish justification of suffering from hope.

context.title: Satirical speed
context.text: Catastrophes arrive with implausible frequency. The compression exposes explanatory habits rather than offering realistic travel chronology.
context.takeaway: Attend to the repeated argument beneath the incidents.

notice.text: Notice explanations that survive any evidence.
notice.why: Their flexibility may reveal an inability to learn.
The practical response to suffering is repeatedly at stake.

opening: Candide has been taught that he lives in the best of all possible worlds. Expelled from the house where he grew up, he encounters war, persecution, and an earthquake, while the philosophy meant to explain his good fortune proves equally capable of explaining everybody’s suffering. Voltaire sends this earnest pupil through one disaster after another in a comedy whose cruelty falls as much on the explanations as on the victims. Candide keeps trying to believe what experience makes increasingly difficult to defend.
